and.name: Repair_Technique
and.description: Ground-truth reconstruction of the feature-based classification of model repair approaches, based on the screenshots of the classification feature model and the paper "A Feature-based Classification of Model Repair Approaches".

and.name: Domain
and.description: Domain characterizes the modeling setting assumed by a repair technique, including the formalisms it targets, whether it is meta-model independent, the technical space in which models are defined, and whether the setting is bounded or multi-model.

alt.name: Formalism
alt.description: Formalism captures the family of modeling notations or representations manipulated by the technique, such as logical, object-oriented, relational, or graph-based models.

alt.name: Technical_Space
alt.description: Technical_Space identifies the modeling framework or technological space used to define the models, such as XML, MDA, EMF, or other environments.

and.name: Multi_model
and.description: Multi_model denotes techniques that manage consistency across more than one model and may distinguish controlled-update and pairwise settings.

and.name: Constraint
and.description: Constraint classifies how consistency constraints are specified, what kind of relations they express, and in which structural shape those relations are represented.

and.name: Specification
and.description: Specification captures whether constraints are hard coded, user definable, augmented with repair hints, or distinguished for special treatment such as violation selection.

or.name: Kind
or.description: Kind classifies constraints according to whether they concern a single model, multiple models, or are expressed directly as logical formulas.

or.name: Shape
or.description: Shape captures the mechanism used to represent cross-model relationships and constraints, such as traceability links, consistency relations, transformations, logical formulas, or pattern matching.

and.name: Update
and.description: Update classifies the information about user changes that is available to the repair procedure, including state-based and delta-based representations such as frames, edit sequences, pre-states, and histories.

and.name: Check
and.description: Check captures how consistency checking is integrated with repair, whether the checker is internal or external, whether check-only mode is supported, and what form of reporting is returned to the repair procedure or user.

and.name: Reporting
and.description: Reporting describes the shape of inconsistency information returned by the checker, ranging from simple boolean and counting reports to explicit violation sets, goals, and composite reports.

and.name: Repair
and.description: Repair groups the main design choices of a model repair technique, including the core repair engine, enumeration strategy, repair representation, available edit operations, and semantic guarantees such as totality, correctness, stability, and least change.

or.name: Core
or.description: Core identifies the main repair engine, such as human-centric, rule-based, syntactic, or search-based approaches.

and.name: Enumeration
and.description: Enumeration captures whether the procedure returns one or many repairs, whether the set is complete, how repairs are ordered, and whether ordering is fixed, opaque, parameterized, or refined interactively.

alt.name: Representation
alt.description: Representation distinguishes state-based repairs from operation-based repairs, including whether the output is a repair action or repair plan and whether it is concrete or abstract.

alt.name: Edit_Operations
alt.description: Edit_Operations describes whether the repair engine assumes no explicit edit vocabulary or relies on a fixed or customizable set of edit operations.

and.name: Semantics
and.description: Semantics captures the guarantees expected from repairs, including totality, correctness, stability, and least-change properties.

alt.name: Correctness
alt.description: Correctness refines whether the repair procedure is merely well-behaved, consistency improving, or fully consistent.
